item.title: Inside Limoges City Hall devastated by arson attack
item.description: Work is underway to restore the city hall of Limoges, in central France, which was devastated by an arson attack during riots on October 17. More than €1.7 million has been raised through an online fundraising campaign in the wake of the disaster. Also on the show, the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI has finally been released, with gamers in Oceania among the first to get a taste of the latest instalment in the video game franchise.

item.title: Crimea bridge strike: Fact-checking fake videos of damage after Ukraine's attack
item.description: Ukraine struck the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, but not all the dramatic footage circulating online is real. Multiple AI-generated videos falsely show the bridge collapsed with extensive damage. Some even used branding resembling a Ukrainian news agency to appear credible. While the bridge was indeed struck and damaged, the viral videos were fabricated using AI, as Vedika Bahl explains.

item.title: Bassirou Diomaye Faye excluded from Senegal's ruling party
item.description: In tonight's edition, the political divorce between Senegal's president and the powerful former prime minister and mentor is official. Also, all of Nigeria's states have shown willingness for a push to create their own police forces. And in parts of the continent, conflict and a drop in funding have placed huge pressures on children's learning.

item.title: Reconstruction begins at Limoges City Hall after devastating fire
item.description: It's been a month since the nationwide protests that degenerated in violence across France. The dramatic pictures of the historic City Hall in the French city of Limoges set on fire made headlines worldwide. To the relief of many, the reconstruction work on the building has now begun. Since the fire, donations have poured in and already about 80 percent of the necessary funding has been secured. FRANCE 24's Caitlin Brown reports.

item.title: US Democrats nominate Jeffries to be first Black House speaker
item.description: Hakeem Jeffries is on the cusp of becoming the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives after Democrats elected him their leader Wednesday following a sweeping midterm election triumph. Jeffries faced no declared challenger, although opposition from some newly elected progressives had exposed divisions over how Democrats should wield their newfound power. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson reports from Washington.
